llm.summary: The skill is coherent for summarizing workout recordings, with disclosed optional cloud transcription and exercise-dataset lookup behavior users should understand before use.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the artifacts: read a local recording or transcript, optionally transcribe it, standardize exercise names, calculate durations, and produce a compact workout summary.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The workflow discloses local file inspection, ffmpeg/whisper/curl-style commands, cloud transcription options, and dataset matching; the main caution is that a ready cloud backend may be chosen without an extra privacy confirmation step.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no installer, startup hook, dependency bootstrapper, or hidden setup behavior; the package contains documentation and two Python helper scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Reading workout files, using local shell tools, calling optional transcription APIs, and downloading an exercise dataset are proportionate to the task, but they can involve sensitive audio/transcript data and network access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill tells agents not to save summaries or transcripts unless asked; the matching helper may create a local cache at ~/.cache/strength-training-recording-summary/exercises.json, with no background persistence or privilege escalation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with an agent reading local workout audio or transcript files. Prefer local Whisper for privacy. Before using Groq, OpenAI-compatible transcription, or another cloud provider, confirm that the recording can be sent to that service. If using exercise matching, expect a GitHub dataset download and local cache unless you provide a local dataset path; avoid untrusted --dataset-url values.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: The skill text itself discloses local file reads, helper commands, optional writes, cloud APIs, and dataset use, though the frontmatter does not enumerate permissions separately.
[TP4] expected: The external exercise dataset is directly tied to exercise-name standardization and is explicitly named in the skill; it is a supply-chain consideration, not hidden unrelated behavior.
[SDI-1] expected: The helper's default GitHub download and cache behavior is documented in the workflow and supports matching, but users should know it makes a network request if no local dataset/cache exists.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The arbitrary --dataset-url override is not necessary for the core workflow and should be treated carefully, but it is a user-supplied helper option rather than automatic exfiltration or deception.
[SQP-2] expected: Cloud transcription is purpose-aligned and disclosed, but workout recordings can be sensitive, so agents should ask before uploading audio to Groq, OpenAI-compatible, or other third-party services.
[staticScan] expected: The static scan reported clean with no findings, which is consistent with the inspected artifacts.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry was clean across supplied engines and did not add a negative signal.
